record.original_question: Let omega(t) be a smooth compactly supported function supported in [c1 T, c2 T] with 0 < c1 < c2. Prove that the smoothed fourth moment of the Riemann zeta function satisfies integral over all real t of omega(t) |zeta(1/2 + it)|^4 dt = O(T^(1/2 + theta + epsilon)), where theta is an admissible upper bound toward the Ramanujan conjecture.

evidence.quote: Smoothed fourth moment. Let ω(t) be a smooth compactly supported function supported in [c1 T, c2 T ] where 0 < c1 < c2 . Show that integral omega(t)|zeta(1/2 + it)|^4 dt = O(T^(1/2 + theta + epsilon)) where theta is upper bound in Ramanujan’s conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function. For an automorphic form on $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\theta \ge 0$ denote an admissible exponent toward the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture, i.e. a constant such that every Hecke eigenvalue $\lambda(n)$ of a (cuspidal) Hecke–Maass or holomorphic newform satisfies $|\lambda(n)| \le d(n)\, n^{\theta}$, where $d(n)$ is the divisor function (the Ramanujan conjecture corresponds to $\theta = 0$, while currently $\theta \le 7/64$ is known by Kim–Sarnak).

Fix real constants $0 < c_1 < c_2$, and let $\omega \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ be a smooth function with $\mathrm{supp}(\omega) \subset [c_1 T, c_2 T]$ satisfying the usual derivative bounds $\omega^{(j)}(t) \ll_j T^{-j}$. Prove that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \omega(t)\, |\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2} + it)|^{4}\, dt \;=\; O\!\left( T^{\,\tfrac{1}{2} + \theta + \varepsilon} \right)
\]
as $T \to \infty$, where the implied constant depends only on $\omega$, $c_1$, $c_2$, and $\varepsilon$.
artifact.category_tag: Moments of the Riemann zeta function
artifact.status_search_result: The conjectural bound $T^{1/2+\theta+\varepsilon}$ for the smoothed fourth moment of $\zeta(1/2+it)$ over a dyadic window is equivalent, after subtracting the main term, to the conjectural error term $E_2(T) \ll T^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ under the Ramanujan conjecture ($\theta=0$). The best unconditional bound remains $E_2(T) \ll T^{2/3+\varepsilon}$ (Ivić–Motohashi), with only logarithmic refinements in recent work (e.g. Preobrazhenskiĭ 2025). Thus the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the error term of the fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements in the powers of log T in the known bounds for the error term E_2(T) in the fourth moment asymptotic.
status_evidence.claim: Only refinements in log-powers of the unconditional bound for the fourth moment error term are recent; the square-root level bound remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Shifted fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the smoothed/shifted fourth moment via Motohashi's spectral identity involving Ramanujan-type bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectural square-root cancellation in the fourth moment is linked to Ramanujan-type bounds and is not established.
